head: b2b5e5cb
gate: HTTP/3 concurrent owner races its QUIC receive against the handler command wake and retains a late completed event

commands.h3_concurrent: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter="HTTP/3 continuous concurrent" --summary all

benchmark.workload: weft synthetic-handshake HTTP/3 server, one loopback connection, GET / -> 200 "ok", 10k sequential and 1k x 32-stream batches

notes: The HTTP/3 owner drains handler commands only after its current QUIC receive returns. A full poll_interval therefore appeared once per startResponse and once per writeData, producing ~2x poll latency per request. Command tracing at poll_interval=1ms measured 0.92-1.00ms between submit and drain for both command kinds, while execute itself took 5-45us. command_poll_interval defaults to 100us and is used only while active handlers exist; idle connections keep poll_interval. Sequential H3 improved 8.1x to 261.6us/req. The owner now races Adapter.receive against the command wake with std.Io.Select. A wake cancels the receive; a receive that completes late is retained in pending_events and routed on the next iteration, so a fully processed packet is not dropped. Sequential H3 improved another 4.2x to 62.9us/req (33.6x from the original 2.11ms). The 32-stream batch path remained ~135us/req (117us -> 128us -> 135us across the two steps), confirming the batch gap is not the owner's command poll; the next isolation target is the client batch send loop versus per-packet QUIC response processing. Full HTTP/3 test filter passes 928/928; the H3 concurrent filter passes 161/161; weft's H3 adapter route test passes. HTTP/2 remains at 26.0us sequential and 14.9us per batched request.
